--- title: "Urban Greenspace Analysis — Santiago RM" subtitle: "Outputs and interpretation: thermal exposure, vegetation structure, and soil organic matter" author: "Urban Soil Biophysics Lab — CEDEUS / PUC" date: today format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 3 toc-location: left embed-resources: true code-fold: true code-summary: "Show code" theme: cosmo page-layout: full execute: warning: false message: false --- --- # Part 1 — Satellite thermal comparison > Each data source characterizes thermal exposure differently. SantiagoHOT provides air temperature at three moments of the day at high resolution (~10 m). Landsat 8 provides land surface temperature (LST) at 30 m. MODIS provides LST at 1 km — coarse enough that small parks inherit the thermal signature of surrounding streets. ## 1.1 SantiagoHOT — air temperature (AM · AF · PM) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} am_r <- prep_rast_leaflet("data/stgo-hot/santiago-chile_am_temp_c.tif") af_r <- prep_rast_leaflet("data/stgo-hot/santiago-chile_af_temp_c.tif") pm_r <- prep_rast_leaflet("data/stgo-hot/santiago-chile_pm_temp_c.tif") pal_temp <- colorNumeric("YlOrRd", values(am_r), na.color = "transparent") leaflet() |> basemap_tiles() |> addRasterImage(am_r, colors = pal_temp, opacity = 0.7, group = "AM (07–08 h)") |> addRasterImage(af_r, colors = pal_temp, opacity = 0.7, group = "AF (15–16 h)") |> addRasterImage(pm_r, colors = pal_temp, opacity = 0.7, group = "PM (19–20 h)") |> addLegend(pal = pal_temp, values = values(am_r), title = "Air temp (°C)", position = "bottomleft") |> layer_ctrl(c("AM (07–08 h)","AF (15–16 h)","PM (19–20 h)")) |> setView(-70.65, -33.47, zoom = 11) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: > Temperature peaks at AF (afternoon). The city centre and eastern piedmont sectors consistently show higher temperatures across all three moments. ## 1.2 Landsat 8 — LST deciles (30 m) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ls_r <- prep_rast_leaflet("data/geo-data/landsat_lst_deciles_jan2024.tif") leaflet() |> basemap_tiles() |> addRasterImage(ls_r, colors = pal_decile, opacity = 0.7, group = "Landsat LST deciles") |> addLegend(pal = pal_decile, values = 1:10, title = "LST decile
(1=cool, 10=hot)", position = "bottomleft") |> layer_ctrl("Landsat LST deciles") |> setView(-70.65, -33.47, zoom = 11) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: > At 30 m, Landsat resolves within-park variability. Deciles are computed from the least-cloudy January 2024 image. ## 1.3 MODIS — LST deciles (1 km) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mo_r <- prep_rast_leaflet("data/geo-data/modis_lst_deciles_jan2024.tif") leaflet() |> basemap_tiles() |> addRasterImage(mo_r, colors = pal_decile, opacity = 0.7, group = "MODIS LST deciles") |> addLegend(pal = pal_decile, values = 1:10, title = "LST decile
(1=cool, 10=hot)", position = "bottomleft") |> layer_ctrl("MODIS LST deciles") |> setView(-70.65, -33.47, zoom = 11) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: > MODIS pixels are 1 km² — most plazas and roadsides fall within a single pixel shared with streets, inflating their apparent LST. Parks < 1 ha should be interpreted with caution. --- # Part 2 — NDVI — vegetation vigor ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} nd_r <- prep_rast_leaflet("data/geo-data/NDVI_Santiago_Jan2024_30m.tif") leaflet() |> basemap_tiles() |> addRasterImage(nd_r, colors = pal_ndvi, opacity = 0.8, group = "NDVI") |> addLegend(pal = pal_ndvi, values = c(0, 0.8), title = "NDVI", labFormat = labelFormat(digits = 2), position = "bottomleft") |> layer_ctrl("NDVI") |> setView(-70.65, -33.47, zoom = 11) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: > NDVI from Landsat 8 & 9 (January 2024, 30 m). Values near 0.2 indicate impervious or bare soil; values above 0.5 indicate active canopy. Dense tree cover in Parque Metropolitano (NE) and irrigated parks in Las Condes stand out clearly. --- # Part 3 — Park inventory > MINVU registry for Region Metropolitana (updated 12/07/2022). Parks classified into Urban Parks, Lawn Parks, and Roadsides by name pattern matching. Condition (Good / Poor) joined from the áreas verdes dataset via spatial intersection. ## 3.1 Park type ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} parks_type <- parks_full |> dplyr::select(park_id, name, commune, area_ha, greenspace_type) |> clean_geom() leaflet(parks_type) |> basemap_tiles() |> addPolygons( fillColor = ~pal_type(greenspace_type), fillOpacity = 0.7, color = "white", weight = 0.3, popup = ~sprintf( "%s
%s
%.2f ha
%s", name, commune, area_ha, greenspace_type ), label = ~name, group = "Park type" ) |> addLegend(pal = pal_type, values = ~greenspace_type, title = "Park type", position = "bottomleft") |> layer_ctrl("Park type") |> setView(-70.65, -33.47, zoom = 11) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## 3.2 Park condition (Good / Poor) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} parks_cond <- parks_full |> dplyr::select(park_id, name, commune, area_ha, condition) |> clean_geom() leaflet(parks_cond) |> basemap_tiles() |> addPolygons( fillColor = ~pal_cond(condition), fillOpacity = 0.7, color = "white", weight = 0.3, popup = ~sprintf( "%s
%s
%.2f ha
%s", name, commune, area_ha, coalesce(condition, "No data") ), label = ~name, group = "Condition" ) |> addLegend(pal = pal_cond, values = ~condition, title = "Condition", position = "bottomleft", na.label = "No data") |> layer_ctrl("Condition") |> setView(-70.65, -33.47, zoom = 11) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: > 75 % of parks with condition data are classified as Good (BUEN). Deteriorated parks cluster in lower-income comunas in the south and west. --- # Part 4 — Dynamic World vegetation structure > Woody ratio = (trees + shrubs) / (trees + shrubs + grass) from Google Dynamic World at 10 m resolution. Values above 0.6 = High Woody Cover; below 0.4 = High Herbaceous Cover. ## 4.1 Vegetation group per park ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} parks_veg <- parks_full |> dplyr::select(park_id, name, commune, area_ha, veg_group, woody_ratio, grass_ratio) |> dplyr::mutate( woody_pct = scales::percent(woody_ratio, accuracy = 1), grass_pct = scales::percent(grass_ratio, accuracy = 1) ) |> clean_geom() leaflet(parks_veg) |> basemap_tiles() |> addPolygons( fillColor = ~pal_veg(veg_group), fillOpacity = 0.75, color = "white", weight = 0.3, popup = ~sprintf( "%s
%s · %.2f ha
Woody: %s   Grass: %s
%s", name, commune, area_ha, woody_pct, grass_pct, veg_group ), label = ~name, group = "Vegetation group" ) |> addLegend(pal = pal_veg, values = ~veg_group, title = "Vegetation group", position = "bottomleft") |> layer_ctrl("Vegetation group") |> setView(-70.65, -33.47, zoom = 11) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: > Most Urban Parks fall in the Woody category. The majority of Lawn Parks and Roadsides are Grass or Unclassified, consistent with their management as mowed turf or paved medians. --- # Part 5 — Combined thermal leaflet > All thermal sources on a single map. Toggle between layers to compare how Landsat, MODIS, and SantiagoHOT characterise the same parks. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pal_am <- colorNumeric("Blues", domain = range(centroids_df$temp_am, na.rm=TRUE), na.color="transparent") pal_af <- colorNumeric("YlOrRd", domain = range(centroids_df$temp_af, na.rm=TRUE), na.color="transparent") pal_pm <- colorNumeric("Purples",domain = range(centroids_df$temp_pm, na.rm=TRUE), na.color="transparent") pal_avg <- colorNumeric("RdYlBu", domain = range(centroids_df$temp_mean,na.rm=TRUE), reverse = TRUE, na.color="transparent") pal_ls <- colorNumeric("YlOrRd", domain = 1:10, na.color="transparent") pal_mo <- colorNumeric("YlOrRd", domain = 1:10, na.color="transparent") leaflet(centroids_df) |> basemap_tiles() |> addCircleMarkers(~lon, ~lat, radius = 5, color = ~pal_am(temp_am), fillColor = ~pal_am(temp_am), fillOpacity = 0.85, stroke = FALSE, popup = ~sprintf("%s
AM: %.1f °C", name, temp_am), group = "StgoHOT AM") |> addCircleMarkers(~lon, ~lat, radius = 5, color = ~pal_af(temp_af), fillColor = ~pal_af(temp_af), fillOpacity = 0.85, stroke = FALSE, popup = ~sprintf("%s
AF: %.1f °C", name, temp_af), group = "StgoHOT AF") |> addCircleMarkers(~lon, ~lat, radius = 5, color = ~pal_pm(temp_pm), fillColor = ~pal_pm(temp_pm), fillOpacity = 0.85, stroke = FALSE, popup = ~sprintf("%s
PM: %.1f °C", name, temp_pm), group = "StgoHOT PM") |> addCircleMarkers(~lon, ~lat, radius = 5, color = ~pal_avg(temp_mean), fillColor = ~pal_avg(temp_mean), fillOpacity = 0.85, stroke = FALSE, popup = ~sprintf("%s
Mean: %.1f °C", name, temp_mean), group = "StgoHOT Mean") |> addCircleMarkers(~lon, ~lat, radius = 5, color = ~pal_ls(landsat_decile), fillColor = ~pal_ls(landsat_decile), fillOpacity = 0.85, stroke = FALSE, popup = ~sprintf("%s
Landsat decile: %.1f", name, landsat_decile), group = "Landsat decile") |> addCircleMarkers(~lon, ~lat, radius = 5, color = ~pal_mo(modis_decile), fillColor = ~pal_mo(modis_decile), fillOpacity = 0.85, stroke = FALSE, popup = ~sprintf("%s
MODIS decile: %.1f", name, modis_decile), group = "MODIS decile") |> addLayersControl( baseGroups = c("Light","Satellite","Streets"), overlayGroups = c("StgoHOT AM","StgoHOT AF","StgoHOT PM", "StgoHOT Mean","Landsat decile","MODIS decile"), options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE) ) |> addScaleBar(position = "bottomright", options = scaleBarOptions(imperial = FALSE)) |> setView(-70.65, -33.47, zoom = 11) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: > Agreement between sources is generally high for large parks (> 1 ha). For small plazas and roadsides, MODIS deciles diverge from SantiagoHOT due to the 1 km pixel size. --- # Part 6 — Park characteristics combined > Integrated view of park type, management condition, NDVI, and vegetation structure (woody/grass/mixed). Click any marker for details. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pal_ndvi_pts <- colorNumeric(c("#ece7f2","#41ab5d","#006d2c"), domain = c(0,0.8), na.color="#cccccc") centroids_df <- centroids_df |> dplyr::mutate( popup_chars = sprintf( '%s
%s · %.2f ha
Type: %s
Condition: %s
Veg group: %s
NDVI: %.3f
Woody ratio: %s', name, commune, area_ha, greenspace_type, coalesce(condition, "No data"), veg_group, coalesce(ndvi_mean, NA_real_), scales::percent(coalesce(woody_ratio, NA_real_), accuracy=1) ) ) leaflet(centroids_df) |> basemap_tiles() |> addCircleMarkers(~lon, ~lat, radius = 6, color = ~pal_type(greenspace_type), fillColor = ~pal_type(greenspace_type), fillOpacity = 0.85, stroke = FALSE, popup = ~popup_chars, label = ~name, group = "Park type") |> addCircleMarkers(~lon, ~lat, radius = 6, color = ~pal_cond(condition), fillColor = ~pal_cond(condition), fillOpacity = 0.85, stroke = FALSE, popup = ~popup_chars, label = ~name, group = "Condition") |> addCircleMarkers(~lon, ~lat, radius = 6, color = ~pal_ndvi_pts(ndvi_mean), fillColor = ~pal_ndvi_pts(ndvi_mean), fillOpacity = 0.85, stroke = FALSE, popup = ~popup_chars, label = ~name, group = "NDVI") |> addCircleMarkers(~lon, ~lat, radius = 6, color = ~pal_veg(veg_group), fillColor = ~pal_veg(veg_group), fillOpacity = 0.85, stroke = FALSE, popup = ~popup_chars, label = ~name, group = "Veg group") |> addLayersControl( baseGroups = c("Light","Satellite","Streets"), overlayGroups = c("Park type","Condition","NDVI","Veg group"), options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE) ) |> addScaleBar(position = "bottomright", options = scaleBarOptions(imperial = FALSE)) |> setView(-70.65, -33.47, zoom = 11) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: --- # Part 7 — NDVI associations ## 7.1 NDVI by park type, condition, and vegetation group ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ndvi_df <- centroids_df |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(ndvi_mean)) p_type <- ndvi_df |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(greenspace_type)) |> ggplot(aes(x = greenspace_type, y = ndvi_mean, fill = greenspace_type)) + geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.size = 0.8) + geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.2, size = 0.8) + scale_fill_manual(values = c( "Urban Park" = "#2d6a4f", "Lawn Park" = "#95d5b2", "Roadside" = "#e76f51" )) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean NDVI") + theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1)) p_cond <- ndvi_df |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(condition)) |> ggplot(aes(x = condition, y = ndvi_mean, fill = condition)) + geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.size = 0.8) + geom_jitter(width = 0.12, alpha = 0.2, size = 0.8) + scale_fill_manual(values = c( "Good condition" = "#52b788", "Poor condition" = "#e76f51" )) + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1)) p_veg <- ndvi_df |> dplyr::filter(veg_group != "Unclassified") |> ggplot(aes(x = veg_group, y = ndvi_mean, fill = veg_group)) + geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.size = 0.8) + scale_fill_manual(values = c( "Woody" = "#41ab5d", "Grass" = "#fc9272", "Mixed" = "#9e9ac8" )) + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "none") p_type + p_cond + p_veg + plot_annotation( title = "NDVI by park characteristics", subtitle = "Landsat 8 & 9 — January 2024 (30 m)" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](results_files/figure-html/ndvi-boxplots-1.png){width=1056} ::: ::: > Urban Parks have the highest median NDVI, consistent with larger canopy cover. Good condition parks score slightly higher than poor condition ones. Woody parks unsurprisingly lead in vegetation vigor. ## 7.2 NDVI vs thermal sources ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} vars <- list( list(col="temp_af", lab="AF temperature (°C)", pal="YlOrRd"), list(col="landsat_decile",lab="Landsat decile", pal="YlOrRd"), list(col="modis_decile", lab="MODIS decile", pal="YlOrRd") ) make_scatter <- function(xcol, xlab) { ndvi_df |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[xcol]]), veg_group != "Unclassified") |> ggplot(aes(x = .data[[xcol]], y = ndvi_mean, color = veg_group)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.2) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "gray30", linewidth = 0.7) + scale_color_manual(values = c( "Woody"="#41ab5d","Grass"="#fc9272", "Mixed"="#9e9ac8","Unclassified"="#cccccc" )) + labs(x = xlab, y = "Mean NDVI", color = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.size = unit(0.4,"cm")) } make_scatter("temp_af", "AF temperature (°C)") + make_scatter("landsat_decile", "Landsat LST decile") + make_scatter("modis_decile", "MODIS LST decile") + plot_layout(ncol = 3) + plot_annotation( title = "NDVI vs thermal exposure", subtitle = "Negative slope expected: hotter parks tend to have lower vegetation vigor" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](results_files/figure-html/ndvi-vs-thermal-1.png){width=1152} ::: ::: --- # Part 8 — Field soil organic matter > 59 soil samples from Santiago RM, spatially joined to the nearest MINVU park (nearest-feature, WGS84). Organic matter (OM %) measured in the field. ## 8.1 Map of OM sampling sites ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} if (om_has_data) { pal_om <- colorNumeric("YlGn", domain = om_joined$om_value, na.color="#cccccc") leaflet(om_joined) |> basemap_tiles() |> addCircleMarkers(~lon, ~lat, radius = ~scales::rescale(om_value, to = c(4,12)), fillColor = ~pal_om(om_value), fillOpacity = 0.85, color = "white", weight = 1, popup = ~sprintf( "OM: %.2f %%
Park: %s
Type: %s
Condition: %s
Veg group: %s", om_value, coalesce(name, "—"), coalesce(greenspace_type, "—"), coalesce(condition, "No data"), veg_group ), group = "OM samples" ) |> addLegend(pal = pal_om, values = ~om_value, title = "Organic matter (%)", position = "bottomleft") |> layer_ctrl("OM samples") |> setView(-70.65, -33.47, zoom = 11) } else { cat("dataset_rm_test.csv not found — add to data/geo-data/") } ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: > Marker size proportional to OM value. Higher OM tends to cluster in wooded parks in the eastern sector (Providencia, Las Condes), consistent with higher canopy input and lower soil temperature. ## 8.2 OM associations ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} if (om_has_data) { col_vals <- c("Urban Park"="#2d6a4f","Lawn Park"="#95d5b2","Roadside"="#e76f51") p1 <- om_joined |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(greenspace_type)) |> ggplot(aes(x=greenspace_type, y=om_value, fill=greenspace_type)) + geom_boxplot(alpha=0.7, outlier.size=1) + geom_jitter(width=0.15, alpha=0.5, size=1.5) + scale_fill_manual(values=col_vals) + labs(title="OM by park type", x=NULL, y="OM (%)") + theme_minimal(base_size=10) + theme(legend.position="none", axis.text.x=element_text(angle=20,hjust=1)) p2 <- om_joined |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(condition)) |> ggplot(aes(x=condition, y=om_value, fill=condition)) + geom_boxplot(alpha=0.7, outlier.size=1) + geom_jitter(width=0.12, alpha=0.5, size=1.5) + scale_fill_manual(values=c("Good condition"="#52b788","Poor condition"="#e76f51")) + labs(title="OM by condition", x=NULL, y=NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size=10) + theme(legend.position="none", axis.text.x=element_text(angle=20,hjust=1)) p3 <- om_joined |> dplyr::filter(veg_group!="Unclassified") |> ggplot(aes(x=veg_group, y=om_value, fill=veg_group)) + geom_boxplot(alpha=0.7, outlier.size=1) + scale_fill_manual(values=c("Woody"="#41ab5d","Grass"="#fc9272","Mixed"="#9e9ac8")) + labs(title="OM by veg group", x=NULL, y=NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size=10) + theme(legend.position="none") make_om_scatter <- function(xcol, xlab) { om_joined |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[xcol]]), !is.na(greenspace_type)) |> ggplot(aes(x=.data[[xcol]], y=om_value, color=greenspace_type)) + geom_point(alpha=0.7, size=2) + geom_smooth(method="lm", se=TRUE, color="gray30", linewidth=0.7) + scale_color_manual(values=col_vals) + labs(x=xlab, y="OM (%)", color=NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size=10) + theme(legend.position="bottom", legend.key.size=unit(0.4,"cm")) } p4 <- make_om_scatter("ndvi_mean", "NDVI") p5 <- make_om_scatter("temp_mean", "StgoHOT mean (°C)") p6 <- make_om_scatter("landsat_decile", "Landsat decile") p7 <- make_om_scatter("modis_decile", "MODIS decile") (p1 | p2 | p3) / (p4 | p5 | p6) + plot_annotation( title = "Soil organic matter associations", subtitle = sprintf("n = %d field samples | January 2024", nrow(om_joined)) ) } else { cat("OM data not available.") } ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](results_files/figure-html/om-plots-1.png){width=1152} ::: ::: > Higher NDVI is the strongest predictor of OM in this preliminary dataset, consistent with the expected soil C input from leaf litter. Thermal exposure (StgoHOT, Landsat) shows a negative trend — hotter parks tend to have lower OM, likely through accelerated decomposition. --- *Data: SantiagoHOT (Jan 20, 2024) · Landsat 8 C2 T1 L2 (Jan 2024) · MODIS MOD11A1 (Jan 20, 2024) · Google Dynamic World v1 (Jan 2024 ±5 d) · MINVU Urban Parks (updated 12/07/2022) · Áreas Verdes Santiago · Field sampling 2024.*
